user.title: Area Averages
user.description:
Area Averages gives each area one sensor that averages the sensors in it, and reports which of them are offline, stale or low on battery.

You add averages one at a time and choose which areas get one and what they measure. Auto-discovery can fill the list in for you from the areas you already have.

[Documentation]({docs_url})

data_description.auto_discover: Creates an average for every area that has sensors of the types below, and for new areas as they appear. Each one shows up as its own entry you can edit or delete. Leave this off to add averages by hand.
data_description.auto_discover_classes: Only used while auto-discovery is on. An average you add by hand can be of any supported type.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Area Averages is already configured. Add another average from its entry instead.

init.title: Area Averages options
init.description: These settings apply to every average. To change which sensors go into one average, use the gear icon on its row.

data.stale_hours: Flag a sensor as stale after (hours)
data.exclude_label: Label that excludes a sensor from averages

data_description.auto_discover: Creates an average for every area that has sensors of the types below, and for new areas as they appear. Turning this off leaves the averages you already have; nothing is ever deleted automatically.
data_description.auto_discover_classes: Only used while auto-discovery is on. An average you add by hand can be of any supported type.
data_description.stale_hours: Measured from a member's last numeric report, not from its last change, so a sensor repeating the same value is not stale. Stale members are dropped from the average. A member that has never reported a number is listed as offline instead of stale, because there is no report to age.
data_description.battery_threshold: Members whose device has a battery level at or below this are listed in the issue attribute. Binary low-battery sensors are always reported.
data_description.trend_minutes: How far back the rising / falling / steady reading looks. Held in memory only, so the trend reads unknown for the first quarter hour after a restart.
data_description.exclude_label: Used by averages in exclude mode. The label applies to an entity or to its device. Labelling the device excludes every measurement that device reports. Excluded sensors stay visible on the dashboard under "Not in average"; they are simply not counted.
data_description.ignored: These were discovered once and then deleted, so auto-discovery leaves them alone. Untick one to let it come back.

user.title: Which average?
user.description: Each area gets one average per sensor type, so a bathroom humidity average and a bathroom temperature average are two separate entries.

data_description.area_id: The average is named after this area and is assigned to it, so it shows up on area cards and to voice assistants.
data_description.device_class: Every type has a fixed unit, and members reporting another unit are converted into it.

data_description.mode: Everything in the area keeps following the entity registry, so a sensor you move into the area joins on its own. Only these sensors is a fixed list that ignores anything else in the area.
data_description.include_entities: Only used in include mode. The list offers the sensors of this type that are in this area.
data_description.include_label: Only used in include mode. Anything in the area carrying this label joins the average as well, so you can add sensors without editing this list.

reconfigure.title: Which sensors go in?
reconfigure.description: {average}. To move this average to another area, or change what it measures, delete it and add a new one. Those two things define the average.

data_description.include_label: Only used in include mode. Anything in the area carrying this label joins the average as well, so you can add sensors without editing this list.

error.already_configured: That area already has an average of this type. Edit the existing one instead.

abort.already_configured: That area already has an average of this type.
